notable_absence.finding: Of 132 'Required Sync Gateway RBAC roles:' blocks found across ~155 documented operations, the ONLY endpoints carrying no RBAC role requirement at all are: (1) every endpoint under the Authentication tag - OIDC initiation/callback/refresh, Facebook/Google session creation - and (2) the OIDC mock-provider/testing endpoints at the end of the Unsupported tag, and (3) three bare health/identity probes: 'Get server information' (GET /), 'Check if server online' (HEAD /), and 'Check if API is available' (GET /_ping). All three categories are exactly the surfaces that must be reachable BEFORE an identity is established (login flows, a test double for an external IdP, and liveness checks) - so the absence is structurally coherent with, not a violation of, the pervasive RBAC gate everywhere else, including on every endpoint in the Unsupported tag's debugging/legacy-view surface.

cross_component_finding: This file settles round 27's central open question for the Admin REST API: does the coarse admin-vs-not bypass (sgw:admin-rest-api, sgw:rbac-user) resolve to an actual per-endpoint Server RBAC check, or just to unconditional admin access once past the API boundary? It resolves to a real per-endpoint check: 132 of ~155 documented Admin API operations carry an explicit 'Required Sync Gateway RBAC roles:' block naming one or more of six roles never seen elsewhere in this project's registry - Sync Gateway Dev Ops, Sync Gateway Architect, Sync Gateway Application, Sync Gateway Application Read Only, Sync Gateway Replicator, External Stats Reader - none of which are the generic Cluster Admin/Full Admin/Read Only Admin/Bucket Admin roles already promoted. This does NOT contradict round 27's channel/require*() model, because it is a completely different surface: the sync function's requireUser/requireRole/requireAccess/requireAdmin gate WRITES on the Public API (channel-based, document-scoped), while this RBAC-role gate governs the Admin API (Server-RBAC-based, operation-scoped) - the two systems round 27 already found to have 'no relationship' to each other. What is new here is the finding that the Admin surface's own gate is granular and role-differentiated (six distinct fine-grained roles, not one uniform 'is-admin' bit), and that it reaches across the boundary operationally even though the identity systems remain conceptually disjoint: creating/managing an sgw:role or sgw:user (Public-API, channel-grant objects) itself requires the caller to hold Sync Gateway Architect or Sync Gateway Application (a Server RBAC role) via the Admin API, and 'Create a new user session' (Admin API, POST /{db}/_session) - which mints a Public-API session cookie on behalf of an arbitrary named sgw:user - is itself gated by Sync Gateway Architect/Application ('Required Sync Gateway RBAC roles: * Sync Gateway Architect * Sync Gateway Application', directly above 'A session cannot be generated for an non-existent user or the GUEST user.'). So the 'no relationship' finding holds for AUTHENTICATION (the two systems never share a login) but not for ADMINISTRATION (the Server-RBAC system administers, and can impersonate, the channel-based one). A further granularity nuance: 'Replace database configuration' (PUT /{db}/_config) accepts either Sync Gateway Architect OR 'Sync Gateway Application (sync function only)' - a field-scoped variant of the Application role honoured only for the sync-function portion of a full config replace - while the dedicated 'Set database sync function' endpoint (PUT /{keyspace}/_config/sync) accepts only Architect. This is the first sub-endpoint-granularity RBAC scoping found in the corpus.
cross_product_finding: The requiresServerRole predicate (recurrence 43 pre-existing, per registry) already models this exact pattern for analytics/, backup/ and eventing/'s own admin REST surfaces (role:analytics-manager, role:backup-admin, role:eventing-full-admin) gating their respective admin endpoints - so Sync Gateway's Admin REST API turns out to be one more instance of a project-wide pattern (every Couchbase product's administrative REST surface reuses Couchbase Server's RBAC catalogue to gate itself) rather than a novel mechanism unique to Sync Gateway. What IS unique to this page is the discovery of the actual role catalogue members for Sync Gateway's slice of that shared pattern - six named roles that were previously represented in the registry only abstractly, as sgw:rbac-user's undifferentiated 'reused Server RBAC'.
